reviews.text: The advertisements feel intrusive and draining, and I don’t appreciate how it mixes in dark patterns to get you to use the app, even though some parts are useful. If it switched to using less invasive and coercive methods of asking for my money or advertising features, I’d be more inclined to pay for it. For example, offer me 24 non consecutive hours of studying on a + plan instead of a free trial with automatic recurring payments. I would much rather have an option to pay for individual sessions rather than a subscription. When companies use tricky tactics, it makes me so angry that I start looking for alternatives and calling my local representatives asking them to create stricter regulations for companies like this.

I’m now seeing that other individuals in the reviews have experienced sudden crashes that delete their whole set. We spend hours on these sets and pay money we worked hard for to hopefully keep the app running up to par. Then, my definition for my previous card very frequently gets deleted when I press add card. What the. Then they used to remove the blank cards so you didn’t have to manually do it yourself because who needs a BLANK flashcard, well now I guess Quizlet decided you do need that blank card. I pay way too much money for a flashcard app, let alone one that’s annoying and overly tedious. I also hate where the new add button is because I always accidentally press save set—frustrating and it makes it harder to add a lot of cards quickly. This is on my iPad by the way and I am unsure how it does with a phone or a browser.

reviews.title: Horrible customer service
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with both the customer service and refund process. I accidentally forgot to cancel my free trial before it renewed, and instead of receiving any understanding or flexibility, I was repeatedly sent back and forth between Quizlet and Google Play. Google told me to contact Quizlet, while Quizlet repeatedly claimed they couldn’t help because the purchase was made through Google Play.

No one took ownership of the issue, and I received the same copy-and-paste responses over and over again. As a customer, it’s incredibly frustrating to be caught between two companies, each pointing the finger at the other while offering no real assistance.

Mistakes happen, and many companies offer a one-time courtesy refund for accidental renewals. The complete lack of empathy or willingness to review my case has left me with a very negative impression of the service.

I won’t be subscribing again, and I wouldn’t recommend purchasing through Google Play if you expect any support should something go wrong.

reviews.title: Quizlet in 2026: Why are you still ignoring Spaced Repetition?
reviews.text: As a long-time user, I’m honestly starting to rethink sticking with this app. It’s 2026, yet Quizlet still lacks a proper Spaced Repetition system, the very feature that has made platforms like Anki the gold standard for anyone actually serious about learning. Ignoring this isn’t just a minor oversight, it’s a massive strategic blunder that’s handing your competitors a huge advantage. Students don’t just want flashcards anymore they want a proven, algorithmic way to master information efficiently, which is exactly what Anki delivers. Your motto is “Get better marks,” but how can you claim that while missing the most scientifically backed tool for retention? Adding Spaced Repetition is the only way to keep us from jumping ship to the apps that are actually evolving. It’s time to catch up.
